title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages. 𝔊 is a profinite group topologically generated by a pair (ρ,σ). The margin of the next page says ρ^3=1 and σ^2=1. So 𝔊 is a quotient of the 'universal' group 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3}, presumably Ẑ/3 * Ẑ/2, the profinite completion of PSL2(Z).

To the pair (ρ,σ) Grothendieck has attached several groups:
- B_{ρ,σ}: a group of automorphisms of 𝔊 adapted to (ρ,σ). By the next page its elements are parametrised as u_{α,β,γ} with α,β,γ ∈ 𝔊.
- Z_ρ and Z_σ: centralisers, or related groups, of ρ and σ.
- G_{ρ,σ} = B_{ρ,σ}·𝔊: a group containing B and the image of 𝔊, mapping to γ_{ρ,σ} via δ_G.
- S_0M^0_𝔊: a 'fibered product' subgroup of quadruples (u,a,b,U) ∈ B×Z_ρ×Z_σ×G satisfying compatibilities like (76): δ_ρ(a)=δ_σ(b)=δ_G(U) in γ_{ρ,σ}.
- M_{ρ,σ}: a quotient of S_0M^0_𝔊.

In the universal case (next page, (90)) these become Grothendieck's Teichmüller-type groups: B' = M'^~_{0,3}[0], G' = M'^~_{0,3}, Γ = Γ'^~_Q. The previous page builds the universal map Ψ_G : M'^~_{0,3} → G_{ρ,σ} attached to a 'realisation' Ψ: 𝔊^{+∧}_{0,3} → 𝔊.

This page restates the construction as a functoriality statement. Take a surjective homomorphism φ: 𝔊 → 𝔊' with φ(ρ,σ)=(ρ',σ'). Then there is a unique homomorphism φ^0_{SM}: S_0M^0_𝔊 → S_0M^0_{𝔊'} such that:
- (a) It is induced componentwise by homomorphisms φ_B: B_{ρ,σ}→B_{ρ',σ'}, φ_ρ: Z_ρ→Z_{ρ'}, φ_σ: Z_σ→Z_{σ'} and φ_G: G_{ρ,σ}→G_{ρ',σ'}.
- (b) (Partly struck out.) φ_{SM} induces φ_G.
- (c) The square 𝔊→G_{ρ,σ}, 𝔊'→G_{ρ',σ'} commutes with φ and φ_G. Since G = B·𝔊, φ_G is determined by φ_B.
- (d) For u ∈ B_{ρ,σ} and u' = φ_B(u), φ∘u = u'∘φ. Since φ is surjective, this determines u' from u, so φ_B, hence φ_G, φ_{SM} and the quotient map φ_M: M_{ρ,σ}→M_{ρ',σ'}, are all determined by φ.

The next page gives the explicit formula u_{α,β,γ} ↦ u_{φ(α),φ(β),φ(γ)}. It then specialises to 𝔊 = universal case, to recover the earlier theorems 'in slightly more precise form'. The marginal note on this page already suggests reversing the roles: a map from the universal object to 𝔊, a 'specialisation of 𝔊'.

Purpose: to make the attachment 𝔊 ↦ M_{ρ,σ} (a GT/Teichmüller-type group attached to each two-generated quotient) into a functor on the category of marked quotients of Ẑ/3*Ẑ/2. The universal group M'^~_{0,3} and its action then appear as the value at the initial object, compatible with all specialisations.
errors: The existence of u' in (d) requires u ∈ B_{ρ,σ} to preserve ker φ. This is automatic only if the elements u_{α,β,γ} are defined by 'universal' formulas in the parameters α,β,γ, as the next page's formula (88) suggests. The page asserts existence without stating this. It is a gap rather than an error, given the presumed definition of B via parameters.
(b) is largely struck out and garbled. The logical dependence ('φ_SM determines φ_G' versus 'φ_G is determined by φ_B') is stated redundantly between (b) and (c).

ideas.what: Functoriality, under surjections of marked profinite groups (𝔊,ρ,σ)→(𝔊',ρ',σ'), of the Teichmüller-type groups S_0M^0 and M attached to a marked two-generator quotient of Ẑ/3*Ẑ/2, with the universal case as initial object
ideas.modern_name: Functor from marked finite/profinite quotients of PSL2(Z)^ to GT-like groups; closest modern analogue: the groupoid of GT-shadows (Dolgushev et al.) and actions of GT on Hurwitz-type data
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; GT-shadows: Dolgushev, Khoroshkin, Rogers (c. 2020–2023)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the GT/Teichmüller tower philosophy; this explicit construction appears unpublished

ideas.what: Descent of automorphisms u ∈ B_{ρ,σ} along φ (commutative square (86)), so that φ_B is determined by φ
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of automorphisms with quotients (characteristic or 'universally defined' automorphisms)

missed.claim: Grothendieck attaches to each marked quotient (𝔊,ρ,σ) of Ẑ/3*Ẑ/2 a group M_{ρ,σ}, functorial in surjections, built from parameters (α,β,γ) with u_{α,β,γ} ↦ u_{φ(α),φ(β),φ(γ)}. The universal case recovers his Teichmüller-type group M'^~_{0,3}. This anticipates the recent 'GT-shadows' approach: finite-level approximations of GT, attached to finite quotients and compatible under quotient maps.
missed.quote: On peut reprendre tout ceci comme un énoncé de fonctorialité des constructions faites ... Il y a alors un unique homomorphisme S_0M^0_𝔊 → S_0M^0_𝔊'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing Grothendieck's finite-level groups M_{ρ,σ} with GT-shadows could give an independent, possibly different, finite approximation scheme for GT and Ĝ T. It might also suggest which quotients ('specialisations') carry genuine Galois information.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine functoriality statement. But it documents an unpublished framework of GT-type groups attached functorially to every marked two-generator quotient. This resembles very recent work (GT-shadows) and is not in Grothendieck's circulated texts.
transcription_corrections: Left top margin likely reads 'il conviendrait mieux de prendre 𝔊' →φ 𝔊 [i.e. 𝔊 a] spécialisation de 𝔊'', consistent with (89) on the next page ('interchanger le rôle de 𝔊 et 𝔊'').
Left middle margin: 'ceci montre que φ_SM est déterminé de façon unique en fonction des φ_B, φ_ρ, φ_σ, φ_G'.
(84) line: roughly '(ce qui montre que la connaissance [de φ_SM entraîne celle de] la première: celle de φ_G)'; the struck-out 'induisant' precedes φ_G.
Condition a): 'φ_SM provient des homs' (struck 'φ_M' before it).
